title: Introduce unit-slate autotuner: templated batch/cache defaults + tenant-aware quant fallback
author: Aisha Patel
commits: a1f3d2c: initial unit-slate autotuner skeleton and interfaces
b7e4c9a: add templated defaults YML and validation layer
c3d1f8e: tenant-aware quant fallback orchestration and API surface
d8a7b6f: unit + integration tests for autotuner and policy evaluator
e2f9a1b: telemetry hooks, dashboards and docs for ops
f4b2c33: fix race condition in cache-default reconciliation (followup)
g9c8d55: squash: tidy comments and changelog entry
description:
Motivation: configuring per-tenant batching/caching/quantization defaults is a frequent support surface. Teams repeatedly create ad-hoc defaults that either over-provision (high cost) or under-provision (high latency/failed SLOs). This PR introduces the 'unit-slate autotuner'—a templated, tenant-scoped defaults engine that proposes and enforces economical batch/cache defaults and a graceful quantization fallback policy tied to unit-econ windows.

What this changes (single-string summary): adds a core autotuner engine (policy evaluation + reconciliation loop), a declarative templates format for 'unit slates' (configs/economy/unit-slate-templates.yaml), a tenant-aware quant fallback orchestrator that selects pre-validated quant profiles based on a tenant's recent unit economics and latency sensitivity, telemetry for decision tracing, and an operator-facing docs page + examples.

Design notes: the autotuner runs as an idempotent reconciler that: (1) samples per-tenant recent token cost and p95 latency (via existing telemetry API), (2) scores candidate slate templates (cost/latency/regret heuristics), (3) proposes a delta to tenant defaults and writes a suggested default to the tenant-settings store (requires operator approval for high-impact changes), (4) if the tenant opts into autopilot, the reconciler applies safe rollouts with canary tenants and automatic rollback on quality regressions. Quant fallback is implemented as a staged policy: prefer lossless/low-quant profiles when p95 < threshold OR when model quality signals drop; otherwise step down to compact quant profiles with KV-cache preservation.

Operational safeguards: changes are gated by a conservative safety policy (configs include 'min_latency_floor' and 'max_cost_increase_pct'). Autopilot must be enabled per-tenant. All decisions emit traceable telemetry (reason, score, before/after slate) so SRE and support can audit and revert.

Testing & benchmarks: included unit tests and an integration harness that runs synthetic tenant workloads (0.1 RPS–50 RPS) against the reconciler. On our internal perf rig, the default 'economy-slate-small' reduced token-cost/unit by ~14% for chat-like workloads with <1% quality deviation measured by existing eval harness; prefill-heavy workloads saw 6–9% savings. All tests + lint passed in CI on final run.

Compatibility & rollout: backward-compatible defaults by design—existing tenant defaults are left unchanged unless autopilot is enabled. The new proto adds optional fields and has server-side defaults for older clients. No breaking API changes.

Notes for reviewers: pay attention to race handling in policy_evaluator.go around parallel score computations (I added a fix in the final commit). The templates YML is intentionally small and documented with examples. I recommend reviewing the telemetry traces dashboard to validate decision reasoning.

Related: ENG-2742 (unit-econ templating), ENG-2798 (quant fallback design), SUP-10234 (support ticket motivating tenant autopilot).
